newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banker sees stern test for branch system.
newsitem.headline: German banker sees stern test for branch system.

text.p: Underperforming branches in Germany's banking sector will face closure or consolidation from next year onwards, a top German banker warned on Tuesday.

"The domestic branch system is facing a crucial test," Martin Kohlhaussen, chief executive of Germany's third largest bank, Commerzbank AG, said in an article written for the Boersen-Zeitung newspaper.
"Clearly nobody is considering withdrawing from the area, but on cost-utility grounds, unprofitable branches will face consolidation or closure," he added.

Kohlhaussen said the arrival of the single European currency in 1999 and the wider globalisation in the sector would increase competition in the German market, while offering opportunities to German banks in international markets.
Commerzbank in November launched a major questionnaire among its customers in a move seen as part of a move by German banks to become more efficient and reassess their cost-laden branch networks.
